description: Common JVM error / stack-trace patterns for the jvm skill demo.

patterns.name: NullPointerException
patterns.common_cause: Dereferencing a null reference — often from an unchecked Optional.get(), a missing autowire, or a deserialization that produced null fields.
patterns.typical_fix: Add a null check or Optional.orElseThrow() at the call site; for Spring beans verify @Autowired / @Component scanning is set up.

patterns.name: OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space
patterns.common_cause: Unbounded collection growth (caches without eviction, accumulating List<?> in batch jobs) or oversized request payloads bypassing pagination.
patterns.typical_fix: Add bounded LRU cache (Caffeine), enforce pagination, raise -Xmx only as a stop-gap. Take heap dump with -XX:+HeapDumpOnOutOfMemoryError and analyse with Eclipse MAT.

patterns.name: OutOfMemoryError: Metaspace
patterns.common_cause: Classloader leak — typical in app servers that hot-redeploy WAR/EAR, or in apps that dynamically generate proxies (CGLIB, Groovy, JSP recompile).
patterns.typical_fix: Raise -XX:MaxMetaspaceSize as a temporary measure; root-cause: take heap dump, look for duplicate classloaders. Restart cadence as a stop-gap.

patterns.name: StackOverflowError
patterns.common_cause: Unbounded recursion — frequently an accidental cycle in equals/hashCode/toString between bidirectional JPA associations, or a misconfigured Jackson serializer.
patterns.typical_fix: Add @JsonIgnore on the back-reference, or use @JsonManagedReference / @JsonBackReference. For business recursion, switch to iteration with an explicit stack.

patterns.name: Thread deadlock (jstack)
patterns.common_cause: Two threads acquire two locks in opposite order — common when JDBC connection pool lock and an application-level lock are nested.
patterns.typical_fix: Enforce a global lock-acquisition order, or use tryLock with timeout. Take periodic jstack snapshots to confirm the cycle.

patterns.name: ConcurrentModificationException
patterns.common_cause: Mutating a collection while iterating it from the same thread (fail-fast iterator), or sharing a non-thread-safe collection across threads.
patterns.typical_fix: Use Iterator.remove(), CopyOnWriteArrayList, or take a defensive copy before iterating. For multi-threaded use, switch to ConcurrentHashMap.

patterns.name: ClassNotFoundException / NoClassDefFoundError
patterns.common_cause: Missing dependency at runtime that was present at compile time (excluded by transitive dep resolution), or duplicate JARs with conflicting versions.
patterns.typical_fix: Run mvn dependency:tree / gradle dependencies, ensure the required JAR is in the runtime classpath. For shadow/uber-jars, check the merged manifest.

patterns.name: ClassCastException
patterns.common_cause: Unsafe downcast of a generic type at runtime (type erasure hides the mismatch at compile time), or returning a proxy where the caller expects the concrete class.
patterns.typical_fix: Use instanceof + pattern variables (Java 16+), avoid raw types. For Spring AOP proxies, use interface types or enable CGLIB proxying.

patterns.name: Thread BLOCKED on monitor
patterns.common_cause: Many threads waiting on the same monitor — typical hotspot is a synchronized block guarding a slow I/O call (DB query, HTTP request).
patterns.typical_fix: Move I/O outside the synchronized region; consider ReadWriteLock or per-key striped locks. Profile with async-profiler to identify the contended monitor.

patterns.name: OutOfMemoryError: GC overhead limit exceeded
patterns.common_cause: JVM spending > 98% of time in GC but reclaiming < 2% heap — usually slow heap leak under steady traffic.
patterns.typical_fix: Same as Java heap OOM — identify retention path via heap dump. As a workaround, disable the check with -XX:-UseGCOverheadLimit, but it just delays the crash.
